- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model tends to underestimate; increase downward bias or adjust for mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction to prevent overreaction.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., rapid drop from high peak), model often fails to recognize it; add a “reversion buffer” to forecast.
- If forecast is rising steadily but true outcome shows early decline, model may be lagging; adjust for sentiment shift or add early warning signal.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is mixed or volatile, model tends to overfit recent trends; smooth forecast or use sentiment-weighted average.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “0.50” values, model may be under-reacting; increase sensitivity to sentiment signals.
- When true outcome is below 75% of recent high, model often ignores downward pressure; add a “floor” or “support” rule to prevent excessive overestimation.
